architecture_root_cause: The web application improperly handled database queries in human.aspx via user-controlled HTTP request headers (specifically the X-siLock-Session-Info header or guestaccess.aspx parameters) which were directly concatenated into dynamic SQL queries without parameterized binding.
verification_strategy: Send controlled, non-destructive probe verifying whether custom session header values alter database lookup behavior or generate differential response timing.
remediation: Apply vendor security patch; replace dynamic string interpolation in session handling with strongly-typed parameterized prepared statements; enforce strict header sanitization.

architecture_root_cause: The plugin exposed an unauthenticated endpoint at /wp-content/plugins/wp-automatic/inc/csv.php that accepted a query parameter 'q' which was passed directly into $wpdb->query() without escaping or using prepared statements.
verification_strategy: Test whether providing a harmless SQL boolean expression in the 'q' parameter yields differential CSV output or an empty result versus a syntax exception.
remediation: Update to version 3.92.1 or newer; restrict unauthenticated direct access to script files; utilize $wpdb->prepare() for all database interactions.

architecture_root_cause: The NQL (Not Quite Lucene) filter parser in Ghost backend failed to sanitize nested filter clauses containing specific operators, leading to unescaped query parameter injection into the Knex.js query builder.
verification_strategy: Send differential NQL filter queries with balanced vs unbalanced delimiters and measure response differences.
remediation: Upgrade Ghost to 5.59.1 or above; validate NQL AST before generating Knex queries; enforce strict property allowlists in filter parser.

architecture_root_cause: Unauthenticated access to administrative logging route accepted unescaped input that was concatenated into audit database queries before session validation.
verification_strategy: Measure differential response codes when supplying valid vs malformed character sequences in authentication audit fields.
remediation: Update CWP to the latest release; enforce authentication before database logging; use prepared statements across all administrative logging scripts.
